text_blocks.snippet: Blood clot symptoms vary depending on the location of the clot, but common signs include pain, swelling, and warmth in the affected area. Other symptoms can include shortness of breath, chest pain, and dizziness, with specific symptoms also depending on whether the clot is in the heart, lungs, brain, or elsewhere.

list.title: Leg or Arm:
list.snippet: Gradual or sudden pain, swelling, warmth, and redness are common in the affected limb, usually the lower leg or arm.

list.title: Brain:
list.snippet: Sudden, severe headache, seizures, weakness on one side of the body, difficulty speaking, and vision problems may indicate a blood clot in the brain.

list.title: Heart:
list.snippet: Chest pain, shortness of breath, and pain radiating to the left arm are potential signs of a heart attack caused by a blood clot.

list.title: Lungs:
list.snippet: Increased heart rate, pain with deep breathing, rapid breathing, and shortness of breath can be symptoms of a pulmonary embolism (blood clot in the lungs).
